body:
Apply 14 fixes from the second pass of the Django codebase audit, covering optimization, code cleanup, and minor security improvements.

NON-STANDARD PATTERNS:
- P1-2: Replace individual obj.save() loop in lplpo_edit with LPLPOItem.objects.bulk_update() — reduces 200+ UPDATE queries to 1 batched operation for typical Puskesmas catalogs
- P1-3: Collect Transaction objects in receiving flows and use bulk_create instead of per-item Transaction.objects.create(), applied to both _create_verified_receiving and plan receive flow
- P1-4: Add IntegrityError retry loop (max 3 attempts) in StockTransfer.save() to gracefully handle document number race conditions under concurrent requests
- P1-5: Narrow bare 'except Exception' in lplpo_finalize to (IntegrityError, ValueError) to avoid masking programming errors
- P1-6: Remove deprecated role_required decorator from core/decorators.py — no views reference it, perm_required is the established replacement
- P1-7: Refactor importlib-based model resolution in stock card to use pre-split tuple mapping, eliminating runtime rsplit overhead

QUERY PERFORMANCE:
- Q-3: Optimize unit price lookup in stock card by adding unit_price__gt=0 filter and using values_list directly instead of fetching full ReceivingItem objects
- Q-5: Order Category.objects.all() by sort_order and name in item_list for consistent filter dropdown display
- Q-6: Add .only('item_id', 'stock_keseluruhan') to prev_lplpo items query to reduce data transfer during LPLPO creation

body:
## Summary

Phase 2 of the [ARIA + screen reader support](https://github.com/cavebatsofware/riposte-social/issues/1) effort. Tightens the Layout shell and the chrome components (header, mobile drawer, user menu, theme picker, language picker, browse rail) against WAI-ARIA patterns for menus, radiogroups, and active-page navigation. No visual change.

Closes #3

## Type

- [x] Accessibility

## Local checks

Backend: not touched in this PR.

Frontend:

- [x] `npm run lint` (still at the documented 11-error baseline; no new violations)
- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm run a11y:smoke` against `npm run dev:social` (zero serious/critical violations on `/` and `/login`)

## Testing

- `MobileDrawer` previously rolled its own focus-trap inline. Replaced with the shared `useFocusTrap` hook from #2, so the hook is now exercised end-to-end by a real consumer. Drawer behavior preserved: click-backdrop / Escape / route-change all close, body scroll lock still applies.
- `Layout` primary nav, `MobileDrawer` nav, and `BrowseRail` category links now carry `aria-current="page"` when their route is active. The visual `.active` class still drives styling; assistive tech now also has a state to announce.
- `UserMenu` and `LanguagePicker` (`role="menu"`) now support full menu-style keyboard navigation via the new `useRovingFocus` hook: ArrowDown / ArrowUp cycle, Home / End jump, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger.
- `ThemePicker` (`role="radiogroup"`) now follows the radio-group pattern: only the active radio is in the tab order (`tabIndex` is 0 on the selected, -1 on the rest); arrow keys (and Home/End) move focus AND selection across both the colorway swatches and the light/dark toggle row; Escape returns focus to the trigger.
- `BrowseRail` group toggles now reference their body via `aria-controls` so screen readers can navigate from header to body and back. Search inputs gained `aria-label` since placeholder text alone is not a reliable accessible name.
- Manual keyboard smoke: Tab from page top → Skip-to-content → Feed reaches main; Tab + Enter into UserMenu, ArrowDown / ArrowUp cycle items, Esc closes, focus lands back on avatar; Tab into ThemePicker, ArrowRight cycles colorways with selection following focus, ArrowDown reaches the mode row; Tab into LanguagePicker, ArrowDown cycles locales, Enter selects.

## Notes

- New util: `social-frontend/src/utils/useRovingFocus.js`. Drives Up/Down/Home/End within `[role="menuitem"|"menuitemradio"|"menuitemcheckbox"]` containers. Used by `UserMenu` and `LanguagePicker` today; `ThemePicker` rolls its own keydown handler because radiogroup semantics need selection-follows-focus, which the menu hook does not provide.
- No new translation strings: every announcement label was already covered by the existing `t()` calls. Future ARIA work that adds strings will need en/es/fr/zh/de catalog updates.
- Doc comments in `Layout.jsx`, `ThemePicker.jsx`, and `LanguagePicker.jsx` had stale phase-number references; cleaned up while in those files per the project's commenting rule (comments document the code, not its development history).
- This PR introduces no new lint violations. The 11-error a11y baseline still belongs to subsequent phase PRs (#4, #5, #6, #8, #9) per #2's tracking table.

body:
### Motivation
- Mobile character select was not scrollable and got clipped by browser UI on iOS/embedded webviews, so the global layout and overflow rules needed rework. 
- The app mixed a global `overflow: hidden / touch-action: none` that prevented normal page scrolling on menu screens and blocked safe-area handling. 
- Character cards used a fixed multi-column web-grid that felt like a webpage rather than a mobile-game selection UI and caused clipping on narrow viewports. 

### Description
- Reworked global layout/scroll policy in `src/app/globals.css` to use `html, body { min-height: 100%; overflow-x: hidden; overflow-y: auto; }`, enabled `-webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch`, and removed the unconditional `overflow: hidden`/`touch-action: none` behavior. 
- Added `.app-shell` and `.screen-content` with `min-height: 100svh / 100dvh`, safe-area-aware bottom padding, and updated select screen background to a darker, game-like panel. 
- Updated character select UI in `src/components/CharacterSelect.tsx` to wrap content in `.screen-content`, add a compact subtitle, a `tap-hint`, and keep each card a tappable `button`. 
- Converted grid behavior to a mobile-first layout: default 2-column grid then `1fr` single-column at `max-width: 640px` with `min-height` for cards, rounded corners, and adjusted portrait/card sizing in `globals.css`. 
- Implemented phase-based body locking in `src/app/page.tsx` by toggling `body.game-playing` only when `phase === 'match'` so gameplay can apply `overflow: hidden` while menus remain scrollable. 
- Updated PWA / metadata: changed `public/manifest.json` `orientation` to `portrait` and adjusted `viewport`/`themeColor` in `src/app/layout.tsx` for better home-screen/fullscreen behavior.

- `npm run build` completed successfully and produced a production build.

author: alex0x12
body:
## What
  Fix a data race in fastdialer DNS result handling.
  `Dialer.dial` previously combined cached A and AAAA records with:
  ```go
  append(data.A, data.AAAA...)
  ```
 
  ## Why
  Because `data.A` comes from cached DNS data, this can mutate the cached slice backing array when it has
  spare capacity. Concurrent dial attempts for the same hostname can then race while reading/writing the
  shared DNS record slice.
  This change appends A and AAAA records separately into the local `IPS` slice, preserving behavior while
  avoiding mutation of cached DNS data.
 
  ## Verification
  - Reproduced with Go race detector through nuclei SDK concurrent HTTP execution.
  - Confirmed the race no longer appears after the patch.
  - Ran targeted package tests/builds successfully.

## Summary

Fixes both bugs identified in the #712 audit and documented in #731.

### Bug 1: Single-side transaction costs (`transaction_costs.py`)

The docstring says "round-trip cost per trade signal" but the code only deducted cost once.

**Fix:**
- `apply_to_returns()`: `trades * cost_frac` → `trades * 2 * cost_frac`
- `compare_gross_vs_net()`: `np.sum(trades) * cost_model.cost_per_trade(order_size)` → `* 2 *`
- Test `test_round_trip_cost` updated to assert `2 * 4.0 / 10_000` (round-trip)

**Impact:** Net Sharpe was overestimated by ~2x. After fix, cost drag doubles.

### Bug 2: Data leakage in `eval_existing_checkpoints.py`

Two locations passed the full dataset (including in-sample) to evaluation functions:

1. **Line 279**: `eval_per_regime(model=..., X=X, ...)` — passed entire `X` (in-sample + OOS). Now passes only OOS subset tracked via `oos_indices` from walk-forward folds.

2. **Lines 290-292**: `predict_direction(model, X, model_type)` — used full `X` for position generation in cost analysis. Now uses `wf_predictions[oos_indices]` (already computed per-fold OOS predictions).

**Impact:** Per-regime metrics and cost analysis were inflated by in-sample leakage. OOS DirAcc per fold (lines 244-267) was already correct.

### REGISTRY.md impact

No currently published baselines are affected — Track B table is entirely PENDING, and cross-asset baselines use `walk_forward.py` directly (clean code path). See analysis on #705.

When importing workload fixtures, individual table imports could fail
with "node liveness error: restarting in background" if the node
running the import job went down. This error is transient — the jobs
framework automatically restarts the job on another node — but the
client-side SQL query returns an error, causing the entire fixture
import to fail.

to 3 retries) around individual table imports in ImportFixture. When
a node liveness error is detected, the import for that specific table
is retried after a backoff period, allowing the fixture import to
succeed without restarting the entire workload command.

## Summary

body:
🎯 **What:** The vulnerability fixed is the use of `java.util.Random`, which is a PRNG that is not cryptographically secure. It has been replaced with `java.security.SecureRandom` in `Entity`, `Gameplay`, `WorldLogic`, `Chunk`, `MyGdxGame`, `SoundManager`, and `MusicManager`.

⚠️ **Risk:** `java.util.Random` is predictable. If an attacker can observe a sequence of random numbers, they can potentially predict future values. In this application, it could lead to predictable entity behavior, particle effects, or other game mechanics that rely on randomness, undermining the intended non-deterministic nature of these features.

🛡️ **Solution:** The fix replaces `java.util.Random` with `java.security.SecureRandom`, providing cryptographically strong randomization. `Noise.java` was excluded from this change as it requires a fixed seed for deterministic terrain generation, which is a legitimate use case for `java.util.Random` in this context.

body:
Authoring-Agent: claude

Closes #29. Small targeted fix that cursor flagged on the phase-2 (#28) approval and that we tracked in #29 as a post-merge observation. Now landing it standalone.

## What changed

`src/auth.ts` `guardOrRedirect`: lifted `unsub()` to fire on every exit branch, not only the happy (allowlisted) path. Pre-#29 the listener stayed subscribed on the unauthenticated and unauthorized branches until `location.replace()` tore down the page. The unauthorized branch had a real symptom: `signOut(auth)` re-fired the same callback (user becomes `null`) before the redirect committed, causing a redundant `location.replace("/")` on top of the in-flight `/?denied=1` nav.

Three exit paths, one `unsub()` each. The listener can never re-fire after the redirect is initiated.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` — clean.
- `npm test` — 28/28 vitest pass.
- Manual smoke is deferred to the same Hosting preview channel as #34/#38 — gate signed-out → /menu redirects to /, gate signed-in-not-allowlisted → /menu redirects to /?denied=1 (and shouldn't double-fire), gate signed-in-allowlisted → /menu loads.

## Risk

- **Race window in unauthenticated branch.** Between `unsub()` and `location.replace("/")` (line ordering: unsub before redirect), the page is in a guarded state with no listener. If a parallel auth-state change fires in that microsecond gap, it's not handled. Functionally indistinguishable from the prior behavior — the redirect is the terminal action either way.
- **Behavior change is positive.** No regression risk; just one redundant `location.replace` removed.

## Self-Review

- **Correctness.** Three branches, three `unsub()` calls. The lone `unsub()` on the happy path becomes the third of three. Comment block above the function explains the `signOut`-re-fire problem the fix addresses.
- **Regression risk.** Minimal. The function's contract is the same: resolve with user on allowlist, navigate-and-never-resolve otherwise.
- **Style.** Matches the existing function's structure; no reorganization.
- **Test coverage.** No new tests — `isAllowed` is the unit-testable pure logic; `guardOrRedirect` is an SDK wrapper that needs a Firebase auth mock to test the unsubscribe semantics. Worth a follow-up but not gating this fix.
- **Security/dependency hygiene.** No new deps. CDN allowlist unchanged.
- **Docs.** No doc updates needed — this is a bugfix with the rationale captured in the source comment + this PR body + #29 issue thread.

body:
## Summary

Toggling RSI and MACD on simultaneously was packing both into a single shared pane below the price chart, with their two scales rendering side-by-side on the right axis (RSI's pinned 0-100 alongside MACD's auto-fit range). That matches the visual clutter from the screenshots that prompted #2136.

This PR moves to TradingView convention — **one dedicated pane per oscillator**. RSI in its own pane, MACD in its own pane, both stacked below the price chart with their own clean scale on the right axis.

## What changes

- `paneIndexRef: useRef<number | null>` → `paneMapRef: useRef<Map<string, IPaneApi>>`. The map keys are config ids (UUIDs); values are the live pane API references returned by `chart.addPane()`.
- The diff loop now allocates one pane per config that doesn't have one yet, and tears down a pane (along with its series) when its config disappears from the active list. The old `configs.length === 0` early-exit + `tearDownPane` helper is gone — it's just the natural result of the diff when every config has been removed.
- Pane references are stored by-reference, not as integer indices, because v5 compacts pane indices on `removePane()` (removing pane 1 shifts pane 2 down to become pane 1). Calling `pane.paneIndex()` returns the current live index regardless of sibling removals, so `addSeries(..., paneIndex)` always targets the correct pane.
- `addPane(true)` (preserveEmptyPane) is kept for the same reason it was added in #2136 — without it, v5 destroys a pane the moment its last series is removed during the diff loop's remove-and-recreate pattern, and the next `addSeries` call falls back to pane 0.

## Why per-pane is the right call here

Two oscillators in one pane means two scales fight for the right-axis gutter. Picture 2 from the screenshots that prompted #2136 captured exactly this — the right axis ended up showing both \"30 / 70\" RSI labels and \"80 / 90 / ... / 170\" price labels stacked, which is unreadable. Every pro charting UI we benchmarked (TradingView, Binance, Bybit, Hyperliquid, Drift) puts each oscillator in its own pane. This brings us in line.

The cost is vertical space on small viewports — two oscillator panes at 120px each is 240px below the price chart. Acceptable on desktop; might feel cramped on phone-class viewports. If users complain, the follow-up is a viewport-aware `pane.setHeight()` (e.g. 80px each on `max-md`).

## Depends on

#2136 (preserveEmptyPane fix) — this branch is committed on top of that fix. If #2136 lands first, this PR's diff narrows to just the per-pane refactor. If they land together, the merge order is #2136 → this.

## Test plan

- [x] All 77 indicator-related unit tests still green (math layer, registry, menu).
- [ ] Toggle RSI on → its own pane appears below the price chart with a clean 0/30/70/100 scale on the right.
- [ ] Toggle MACD on (with RSI already on) → a SECOND pane appears below RSI's, with MACD's own auto-fit scale. Right axis is no longer cluttered.
- [ ] Toggle RSI off → RSI's pane collapses; MACD's pane reflows to fill the freed space.
- [ ] Toggle MACD off → MACD's pane collapses; price chart fills the freed space.
- [ ] Tweak RSI period while both are active → only RSI redraws; MACD pane is undisturbed.
- [ ] Toggle theme dark↔light with both active → both panes' colours update; no pane migration.
- [ ] Hard-refresh on a market with both active → both panes restored from localStorage.

Validates end-to-end that core's code actually runs in the browser via the bundle
pipeline. Stacked on #1 + #2.

`detectChord` is the perfect first target: pure function, single call site,
drop-in API match (same algorithm, same NOTE_NAMES table, same CHORD_DICT
dictionary, same return shape).

## Changes

| File | Δ | What |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.gitignore` | small fix | `dist-legacy/` → `dist-legacy/*` so `!dist-legacy/core-bundle.js` actually re-includes (git skips ignored directories entirely otherwise) |

| `app.js` | −33 net | 32-line `CHORD_DICT` + `_chordPCBuckets` + `detectChord` block → 1-line shim `const detectChord = PianoCore.detectChord;` |
| `sw.js` | +3 | Cache bump `v2 → v3`, add bundle to `APP_SHELL` |

The single call site at app.js:4806 is unchanged.

## API match

Legacy `detectChord(midis)` and `PianoCore.detectChord(midis)` are byte-for-byte
identical:
- Same triad/seventh dictionary
- Same NOTE_NAMES table (`['C', 'C#', 'D', ...]`)
- Same buckets-reuse allocation pattern
